sheets.title: Notifications after restoring over a vault's own key — 390 × 844
sheets.caption: A second device seals a vault, connects (so the vault mints a key of its own), then restores an encrypted backup made on the first device. The backup carries its key sealed in the body. Before, the restore kept the device's own key: another principal, and nothing said so. After, the vault takes the backup's key, its old session ends, and the bell says the identity changed.
sheets.before: Notifications none; sheet 390 × 131, "Nothing waiting."; principal differs from the backup's; the old bearer still answers 200
sheets.after: Notifications 1; sheet 390 × 287, card 353 × 174 "Device identity changed"; principal equals the backup's; the old bearer answers 401

sheets.title: Notifications after restoring a backup made before keys travelled — 390 × 844
sheets.caption: The backup was exported before any key existed, so its body carries none. A fresh device restores it. Before, nothing said the principal differs from the backup's. After, one key is minted once and the bell says the backup carried none.
sheets.after: Notifications 1; sheet 390 × 287, card 353 × 174 "Restored without an identity key"; two sessions, one principal

sheets.caption: The same walk at desktop width, where the bell is the statusline key.
